prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments (ideological framing, parties, and individuals omitted)

- Brexit and governance: Pass the negotiated EU exit deal, leave the single market and customs union, end ECJ jurisdiction, and negotiate a UK–EU free trade agreement by December 2020 without extending the transition. Maintain high standards for workers, consumers and the environment. Introduce freeports.

- Economy and tax: Invest in infrastructure while keeping day-to-day spending within fiscal rules (public investment to average ≤3% of GDP; reassess if debt interest >6% of revenue). No rises in income tax, National Insurance or VAT; raise the NI threshold to £9,500 next year. Increase the National Living Wage to two-thirds of median earnings by 2024. Maintain pensioner benefits including the triple lock.

- NHS and social care: Record funding uplift; 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs, 50 million additional GP appointments, 40 new hospitals and 20 upgrades; Innovative Medicines Fund; parity for mental health; free parking for priority groups; clamp down on health tourism (higher surcharge). Social care: £1bn extra each year; cross-party reform; guarantee no one has to sell their home to pay for care; one week’s leave for unpaid carers; double dementia research funding.

- Education and skills: £14bn extra for schools over three years with per‑pupil minimums; raise teacher starting pay to £30,000; SEND funding boost; support for arts, sport and discipline. Create a £3bn National Skills Fund; upgrade FE colleges (~£2bn); 20 Institutes of Technology; require UK apprentices on major projects.

- Policing and justice: 20,000 extra police; stronger stop and search with safeguards; tougher sentences for serious crimes; end automatic halfway release for serious offenders; new knife crime orders; 10,000 more prison places; national cyber crime force; National Crime Laboratory; Police Covenant; Victims’ Law; Domestic Abuse Bill.

- Immigration and integration: Australian-style points system prioritising skills; overall numbers to fall; fast-track routes for NHS staff and top researchers; equal rules for EU and non‑EU; benefits access after five years; higher NHS surcharge; EU residents’ rights guaranteed; stronger English language provision.

- Infrastructure, transport and broadband: Northern Powerhouse Rail (Leeds–Manchester first), Midlands Rail Hub, major road investment, EV rapid-charging within 30 miles for all, consult on earlier petrol/diesel phase‑out, review HS2, restore selected Beeching lines, superbus networks, major pothole fund, cycling fund (£350m), rail reform and contactless ticketing. Gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025 with £5bn for hard‑to‑reach areas.

- Housing and homelessness: Target 300,000 homes a year by mid‑2020s; promote long‑term fixed‑rate mortgages; local discount homes; maintain Right to Buy; reform shared ownership and leasehold; Better Deal for Renters (abolish Section 21 and create a lifetime deposit); Affordable Homes Programme; end rough sleeping by end of Parliament; stamp duty surcharge for non‑resident buyers; infrastructure‑first planning; strengthen building safety; protect and enhance the Green Belt.

- Towns, devolution and local communities: Towns Fund for 100 places; Safer Streets Fund; cultural and community ownership funds; youth services (£500m); extend English devolution (White Paper); City/Growth Deals across the UK.

- Rural and coastal: Replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; farm budget guaranteed for the Parliament; expand seasonal workers scheme to 10,000; leave the Common Fisheries Policy; legal sustainability duties; tackle rural crime; widen broadband/mobile coverage.

- Environment and climate: Net Zero by 2050; £640m Nature for Climate fund (75,000 acres of trees annually by end of Parliament) and peatland restoration; tougher plastics measures, producer responsibility, deposit return scheme, ban exports of plastic waste to non‑OECD; offshore wind to 40GW by 2030; £800m for a carbon capture cluster by mid‑2020s; £500m to decarbonise industry; support hydrogen and nuclear (including fusion); moratorium on fracking unless proven safe; £9.2bn for energy efficiency; stronger air quality laws; £4bn for flood defences; international Blue Planet Fund (£500m).

- Democracy and rights: Repeal the Fixed-term Parliaments Act; update and equalise constituency boundaries; voter ID; curb postal vote abuse; maintain voting age at 18; expand overseas voting rights; online harms legislation; review Gambling Act (e.g., loot boxes). Establish a commission on the constitution, democracy and rights; update judicial review and human rights frameworks while preserving access to justice and security.

- Security, defence and foreign policy: Defence spending above 2% of GDP and rising by at least 0.5% above inflation annually; modernise forces; maintain nuclear deterrent; invest in cyber and create Space Command; support veterans (employer NI relief, childcare, railcard, guaranteed interviews) and curb vexatious legal claims. Maintain 0.7% aid; Magnitsky‑style sanctions; promote girls’ education, media freedom, anti‑trafficking; build UK Holocaust Memorial.

- Trade: Aim for 80% of UK trade under FTAs within three years (including US, Australia, New Zealand, Japan) alongside the UK–EU deal; defend standards (environment, animal welfare, food); protect the NHS in trade talks; Digital Services Tax; support services trade and SME exports; create up to ten freeports.

- Animal welfare: Tougher cruelty sentences; act against illegal puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end excessively long live journeys; extend ivory ban; ban keeping primates as pets; strengthen cat identification measures.
